assessments.reasoning: The verified range in Mozilla's pinned FAQ includes the question and both answer paragraphs. It supports attribution of both propositions to Mozilla. Reading the historical exception alongside section 1.5 explains its scope.

challenge.method: Varied one fact at a time: an exhibit appearing only in the accompanying document, actual attachment by the initial Contributor, and an upgrade from MPL 1.1-only licensing without attachment.
challenge.results: Only the first case rests on the mere presence of an exhibit. Actual attachment changes the premise under section 1.5(a). The upgrade invokes the independent historical ground that Q25 identifies in its final paragraph.

limitations: This records Mozilla's explanation of one scenario. Section 1.5(b) of the governing instrument also reaches versions earlier than 1.1 and asks whether the software was also available under a defined Secondary License.
Q25 supplies no independent normative authority or conclusion about standalone redistribution of the license document.
reasoning: Q25 addresses code shipped with a complete MPL 2.0 document and no per-file boilerplate. Mozilla explains that the exhibit's presence in that copy does not itself attach the notice. Q25 expressly preserves the incompatibility case for code upgraded from MPL 1.1-only licensing.
